text:
Priya: Heads-up — product is proposing a model "turnover" plan to reduce operational surface for old model families. Want engineering and comms input on bench signals, runway, and rollout gates.
Miguel: What do you mean by 'turnover' exactly? retire from hosted only, or full removal?
Priya: Hosted retirement only by default. Dedicated/private customers can keep pinned versions. Turnover triggers we’re considering: sustained eval regressions, security/third-party vuln, or cost-per-token delta >20% vs successor.
Connor: For benches we should pick both quality and performance signals. Proposal: 95th pct token latency, 90/95 token generation latency, and task-specific quality delta (e.g., ROUGE / exact-match) — require quality delta <2% to consider replacement.
Anjali: Comms/contract ask: recommend 90d notice for hosted customers, 180d for customers with enterprise contracts that reference specific model versions. Also include migration assistance offer and a maintained fallback for 6 months.
Priya: Rollout idea: staged switch — canary at 2% traffic for 12h (health + model-quality probes), then 25% for 24h, then 100% over 72h. Abort/rollback if error-rate >1.5x baseline OR latency tail >20% OR eval regression >threshold.
Miguel: Ops question: can we auto-map pinned customers to our closest compatible variant when successor requires different quantization/hardware? Edge case: incompatible tokenizers need manual migration.
release-bot: deploy-campaign created: canary job nextgen-v2 -> 2% traffic. id: dc-9876.
Laura: Draft comms blurb: "We plan to retire hosted access to model X on <DATE>. If you rely on model X, you can pin it in Dedicated/Private or opt into migration assistance. Reach out to support@redwood.com for exceptions." Thoughts? :email:
Priya: Good start. Include an explicit ops playbook link and a migration checklist: 1) run eval harness; 2) compare prompts with new model; 3) run canary traffic; 4) opt-in fallback.
Connor: Action items: I'll publish per-domain eval suites (chat, summarization, code) and a regression-alert config by Thurs. Add synthetic prompt set for latency-sensitive customers.
Miguel: I'll scope bench gating script and an infra flag to mark models as "turnover-eligible". Target prototype by Friday.
Anjali: I'll draft the customer timeline + legal/contract exceptions and a comms cadence (initial notice, reminder at 60d, final at 14d).
Priya: Assignments recorded. If no objections I'll drop this into the public roadmap doc and schedule a decision sync next Tue.
Laura: Also: I can surface a list of customers with pinned versions and export contract dates before the sync.
Priya: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll iterate on the comms template and the bench thresholds in the doc.
